title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Pathway: presentation (newly diagnosed / APL / relapsed) -> workup checklist -> fitness for intensive therapy -> ELN risk by cytogenetics and molecular markers (FLT3/NPM1/IDH/CEBPA) -> biomarker-directed induction (7+3 +/- targeted, CPX-351, or azacitidine-venetoclax) -> response -> risk-directed consolidation / transplant -> surveillance -> relapsed/refractory pathway. No AML-specific dose protocol exists in this library, so treatment leaves give checklist guidance with NO doses and reference no protocol. Structural pathway only; no proprietary guideline text reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison). Leaves are guidance checklists; the physician decides and any dosing is computed elsewhere.

a.text: ELN 2022 genetic risk (favorable / intermediate / adverse) is defined by karyotype plus molecular markers and should be established before consolidation planning; risk can shift with FLT3-ITD allelic ratio and NPM1 status.

b.text: Suspected acute promyelocytic leukemia is a medical emergency: start all-trans retinoic acid on clinical suspicion (before genetic confirmation) and aggressively support coagulopathy - do not wait for cytogenetics.

c.text: Measurable residual disease (MRD) by multiparameter flow or molecular assay refines relapse risk and can inform transplant timing and post-remission monitoring.

d.text: Allogeneic transplant eligibility depends on age, performance status, comorbidity (e.g. HCT-CI), remission status, and donor availability - refer early for intermediate/adverse-risk disease in first remission.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: AML: presentation / disease category
nodes.description: Management branches first by presentation. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Newly diagnosed AML (>= 20% marrow/blood blasts, or an AML-defining genetic lesion)
Suspected acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) - a medical emergency
Relapsed or refractory AML

nodes.name: Workup
nodes.title: Newly diagnosed AML: workup
nodes.description: Confirm diagnosis and gather the genetic and clinical data that drive risk and treatment.
bullets: CBC with differential, peripheral smear, coagulation panel (PT/aPTT/fibrinogen/D-dimer), LDH, uric acid, renal/hepatic panels
Bone marrow aspirate + biopsy: morphology, flow cytometry immunophenotype, cytochemistry
Cytogenetics (karyotype + FISH) and molecular panel: FLT3-ITD/TKD, NPM1, CEBPA, IDH1/IDH2, TP53, RUNX1, ASXL1 (and a broad NGS myeloid panel)
Assess for tumor lysis and hyperleukocytosis/leukostasis; start allopurinol/hydration; leukapheresis if symptomatic hyperleukocytosis
HLA typing and early transplant referral if intensive therapy is a candidate; baseline echocardiogram before anthracycline; HBV/HCV/HIV serology
Lumbar puncture only if CNS symptoms (after excluding leukostasis/coagulopathy)

nodes.name: Fitness
nodes.title: Fitness for intensive induction
nodes.description: The first treatment fork is whether the patient can tolerate intensive (anthracycline-based) induction. Consider age, performance status, organ function, and comorbidity - not chronologic age alone.
bullets: Fit: adequate performance status and organ function for anthracycline-based induction (often younger / limited comorbidity)
Unfit: older and/or significant comorbidity or poor performance status - candidate for lower-intensity therapy

nodes.name: ELN risk
nodes.title: Genetic risk stratification (ELN 2022)
nodes.description: For a fit patient, assign the genetic risk group from karyotype and molecular markers. Risk drives post-remission strategy (chemotherapy consolidation vs transplant).

tables.title: ELN 2022 genetic risk (representative)
rows: t(8;21) or inv(16)/t(16;16) CBF; NPM1-mut without FLT3-ITD; in-frame bZIP CEBPA
NPM1-mut with FLT3-ITD; wild-type without adverse lesions; t(9;11)
Consider allogeneic transplant in first remission
Complex / monosomal karyotype; TP53; ASXL1 / RUNX1; myelodysplasia-related
Allogeneic transplant in first remission if eligible

nodes.name: Induction target
nodes.title: Fit induction: biomarker / disease-type selection
nodes.description: Choose the induction backbone. Targetable lesions and secondary-type disease modify standard 7+3 (cytarabine + anthracycline).

nodes.name: 7+3 + midostaurin
nodes.title: Induction: 7+3 plus midostaurin (FLT3-mutated)
nodes.description: Intensive induction with a FLT3 inhibitor added.
bullets: Standard 7+3 induction (continuous-infusion cytarabine + an anthracycline) plus midostaurin on the specified days
Continue midostaurin through consolidation and as maintenance where used
Antifungal prophylaxis choice must account for azole-FLT3-inhibitor interactions
Reassess response by marrow after count recovery (next step)

nodes.name: 7+3 + gemtuzumab
nodes.title: Induction: 7+3 plus gemtuzumab ozogamicin (CBF / CD33+)
nodes.description: Intensive induction with an anti-CD33 antibody-drug conjugate added for favorable CD33-positive disease.
bullets: Standard 7+3 induction plus fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin (anti-CD33)
Watch for veno-occlusive disease / sinusoidal obstruction, especially if transplant may follow
Core-binding-factor AML is favorable-risk and usually consolidated with cytarabine-based chemotherapy
Reassess response by marrow after count recovery (next step)

nodes.name: CPX-351
nodes.title: Induction: CPX-351 (therapy-related / AML-MRC)
nodes.description: Liposomal fixed-ratio cytarabine-daunorubicin for secondary-type AML in fit patients.
bullets: CPX-351 (liposomal cytarabine-daunorubicin) for therapy-related AML or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes
Expect prolonged cytopenias; give full infection prophylaxis and transfusion support
Most are intermediate/adverse risk - plan early transplant referral
Reassess response by marrow after count recovery (next step)

nodes.title: Induction: standard 7+3
nodes.description: Standard intensive induction when no targetable lesion is present.
bullets: Standard 7+3 induction: continuous-infusion cytarabine for 7 days + an anthracycline for 3 days
Consider a day-14 marrow to assess blast clearance; a second induction if residual leukemia
Full supportive care: neutropenic prophylaxis, transfusion support, tumor-lysis monitoring
Reassess response by marrow after count recovery (next step)

nodes.name: Response
nodes.title: Response assessment after induction
nodes.description: Assess remission by marrow (with MRD where available) after count recovery. Complete remission enables consolidation; failure moves to the relapsed/refractory pathway.

nodes.name: Consolidation
nodes.title: Post-remission (consolidation) strategy by risk
nodes.description: In first complete remission, post-remission therapy is directed by ELN risk and transplant eligibility.

nodes.name: HiDAC consolidation
nodes.title: Consolidation: high-dose cytarabine (favorable risk)
nodes.description: Chemotherapy consolidation, usually without transplant, for favorable-risk disease in CR1.
bullets: Multiple cycles of high-dose cytarabine (HiDAC)
Add the induction-matched targeted agent through consolidation where used (e.g. midostaurin for FLT3, gemtuzumab for CBF)
Monitor cerebellar and ocular toxicity with high-dose cytarabine (neuro checks, steroid eye drops)
Transplant generally reserved for relapse; then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Allo-HSCT (intermediate)
nodes.title: Consolidation: allogeneic transplant (intermediate risk)
nodes.description: Allogeneic transplant in first remission is favored for intermediate-risk disease in eligible patients; otherwise chemotherapy consolidation.
bullets: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant in CR1 for transplant-eligible patients with a suitable donor
If transplant-ineligible or no donor: high-dose cytarabine-based consolidation
MRD status and comorbidity refine the decision; bridge with consolidation while a donor is identified
Then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Allo-HSCT + maintenance (adverse)
nodes.title: Consolidation: allogeneic transplant +/- maintenance (adverse risk)
nodes.description: Adverse-risk disease is consolidated with allogeneic transplant when feasible, with post-remission maintenance and trial enrollment strongly considered.
bullets: Allogeneic transplant in CR1 for eligible patients - the preferred consolidation for adverse-risk disease
Post-remission oral azacitidine maintenance for patients not proceeding to transplant
FLT3-inhibitor maintenance after transplant for FLT3-mutated disease where used
Prioritize clinical-trial enrollment; then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Monitoring after achieving and consolidating remission.
bullets: CBC with differential every 1-3 months for 2 years, then every 3-6 months up to 5 years
Bone marrow / MRD testing for unexplained cytopenias or suspected relapse
Monitor for transplant complications (graft-versus-host disease, infection) where applicable
Survivorship: cardiac follow-up after anthracyclines, vaccination, secondary-malignancy awareness
nodes.linkLabel: If relapse is detected: go to the relapsed/refractory pathway

nodes.name: Unfit therapy
nodes.title: Unfit: lower-intensity therapy selection
nodes.description: For patients not fit for intensive induction, select lower-intensity therapy, directed by molecular markers and frailty.

nodes.name: Azacitidine + venetoclax
nodes.title: Unfit: azacitidine + venetoclax
nodes.description: Hypomethylating agent plus venetoclax is the standard lower-intensity regimen for unfit patients.
bullets: Azacitidine (or decitabine) + venetoclax with a careful ramp-up and tumor-lysis prophylaxis
Antifungal azoles markedly raise venetoclax exposure - reduce the venetoclax dose accordingly
Expect prolonged neutropenia; hold/adjust venetoclax duration by marrow response
For FLT3-mutated unfit disease, this backbone is used and a FLT3 inhibitor is reserved options at relapse
Assess response after the first cycles (next step)

nodes.name: IDH1 inhibitor
nodes.title: Unfit: ivosidenib-based (IDH1-mutated)
nodes.description: An oral IDH1 inhibitor, alone or with azacitidine, for IDH1-mutated unfit disease.
bullets: Ivosidenib + azacitidine (or ivosidenib monotherapy) for IDH1-mutated disease
Monitor for differentiation syndrome and QT prolongation; start corticosteroids promptly if differentiation syndrome is suspected
Azacitidine + venetoclax is an alternative lower-intensity option
Assess response after the first cycles (next step)

nodes.name: IDH2 inhibitor
nodes.title: Unfit: enasidenib (IDH2-mutated)
nodes.description: An oral IDH2 inhibitor for IDH2-mutated unfit disease.
bullets: Enasidenib for IDH2-mutated disease (monotherapy, or with a hypomethylating agent)
Monitor for differentiation syndrome and hyperbilirubinemia
Azacitidine + venetoclax is an alternative lower-intensity option
Assess response after the first cycles (next step)

nodes.name: Low-intensity / BSC
nodes.title: Frail: low-intensity therapy or best supportive care
nodes.description: For the frailest patients or those declining active therapy.
bullets: Single-agent hypomethylating agent (azacitidine or decitabine) or low-dose cytarabine
Best supportive care: transfusions, antimicrobials, hydroxyurea for count control
Early palliative-care involvement and goals-of-care discussion
Assess response / trajectory (next step)

nodes.name: Unfit response
nodes.title: Response after lower-intensity therapy
nodes.description: Assess response after lower-intensity therapy; responders continue on maintenance-style therapy with monitoring, non-responders move to the relapsed/refractory pathway.

nodes.name: APL workup
nodes.title: Suspected APL: emergency workup
nodes.description: APL is a medical emergency dominated by coagulopathy. Start ATRA on suspicion and support coagulation while confirming the diagnosis.
bullets: Start all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) immediately on clinical suspicion - do not wait for genetic confirmation
Confirm PML-RARA by PCR / FISH (and t(15;17) on karyotype); review smear for faggot cells
Aggressively support coagulopathy: transfuse to keep fibrinogen and platelets above threshold; monitor for DIC and bleeding
Avoid procedures (line placement, LP) until coagulopathy is corrected; watch for differentiation syndrome once ATRA starts

nodes.name: APL risk
nodes.title: APL: risk by presenting white-cell count
nodes.description: APL treatment is stratified by presenting white-cell count (a surrogate for risk).

nodes.name: ATRA + ATO
nodes.title: APL, low/intermediate risk: ATRA + arsenic trioxide
nodes.description: Chemotherapy-free ATRA + arsenic trioxide is standard for low/intermediate-risk APL.
bullets: ATRA + arsenic trioxide (ATO) induction and consolidation - no cytotoxic chemotherapy needed
Monitor for differentiation syndrome (treat with corticosteroids) and QT prolongation on ATO
Continue coagulation support until the coagulopathy resolves
Confirm molecular remission (PML-RARA PCR-negative); then surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: ATRA + ATO + cytoreduction
nodes.title: APL, high risk: ATRA + ATO + cytoreduction
nodes.description: High-risk APL adds early cytoreduction to control the white-cell count.
bullets: ATRA + ATO with early cytoreduction (an anthracycline, or gemtuzumab ozogamicin) to control hyperleukocytosis
Aggressive differentiation-syndrome prophylaxis/treatment and coagulopathy support
CNS prophylaxis is considered in high-risk disease
Confirm molecular remission (PML-RARA PCR-negative); then surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Relapsed / refractory
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory AML: pathway
nodes.description: Re-biopsy and repeat molecular testing at relapse (targets can emerge or be lost). Direct therapy by actionable mutation and transplant eligibility, and prioritize clinical trials.
bullets: Repeat marrow with cytogenetics and molecular panel (FLT3, IDH1/2, and emerging targets)
Allogeneic transplant remains the main curative option for chemo-sensitive relapse
Enroll on a clinical trial whenever available

options.label: No target, fit - salvage to transplant

nodes.name: Gilteritinib
nodes.title: Relapsed FLT3-mutated: gilteritinib
nodes.description: A FLT3 inhibitor for relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated disease, as a bridge to transplant.
bullets: Gilteritinib for relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated AML
Monitor for differentiation syndrome and QT prolongation
Bridge responders to allogeneic transplant; consider FLT3-inhibitor maintenance after transplant

nodes.name: Ivosidenib (R/R)
nodes.title: Relapsed IDH1-mutated: ivosidenib
nodes.description: An IDH1 inhibitor for relapsed/refractory IDH1-mutated disease.
bullets: Ivosidenib for relapsed/refractory IDH1-mutated AML
Monitor for differentiation syndrome and QT prolongation
Bridge responders to allogeneic transplant where eligible

nodes.name: Enasidenib (R/R)
nodes.title: Relapsed IDH2-mutated: enasidenib
nodes.description: An IDH2 inhibitor for relapsed/refractory IDH2-mutated disease.
bullets: Enasidenib for relapsed/refractory IDH2-mutated AML
Monitor for differentiation syndrome and hyperbilirubinemia
Bridge responders to allogeneic transplant where eligible

nodes.name: Salvage to transplant
nodes.title: Relapsed, fit: salvage chemotherapy then transplant
nodes.description: Reinduction/salvage chemotherapy in fit patients to achieve a second remission and proceed to allogeneic transplant.
bullets: Intensive salvage chemotherapy (e.g. high-dose cytarabine-based or other multi-agent regimens)
Goal is a second complete remission as a bridge to allogeneic transplant - the main curative option
Add the matched targeted agent if an actionable mutation is present
Donor search / transplant work-up in parallel with reinduction

nodes.name: Trial / BSC
nodes.title: Relapsed, unfit: clinical trial / lower-intensity / supportive care
nodes.description: For unfit patients at relapse, prioritize trials and lower-intensity or supportive approaches.
bullets: Clinical-trial enrollment is preferred
Lower-intensity therapy (hypomethylating agent +/- venetoclax if not previously used)
Best supportive care and early palliative-care involvement per goals of care

nodes.name: APL molecular response
nodes.title: APL: molecular response after consolidation
nodes.description: After ATRA/ATO induction and consolidation, confirm molecular response by PML-RARA PCR. A negative PCR defines molecular remission; a positive or rising PCR signals molecular relapse and pre-emptive salvage.

nodes.name: APL molecular CR
nodes.title: APL: molecular remission - maintenance / surveillance
nodes.description: PCR-negative APL after ATO-based therapy has an excellent prognosis; low-risk disease needs no cytotoxic maintenance and monitoring transitions to surveillance.
bullets: Confirm two sequential PCR-negative marrows to define durable molecular remission
No cytotoxic maintenance is required after ATRA + arsenic trioxide for low/intermediate-risk disease
Serial PML-RARA PCR monitoring for the first 2-3 years; higher-risk disease is monitored more closely
Then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: APL molecular relapse
nodes.title: APL: molecular relapse - pre-emptive salvage
nodes.description: A positive or rising PML-RARA PCR (molecular relapse) is treated pre-emptively, before overt hematologic relapse.
bullets: Confirm on a repeat marrow before acting on a single positive PCR
Arsenic-trioxide-based reinduction (with ATRA) for patients previously in ATO-based remission
Autologous transplant for a second molecular remission; allogeneic transplant if PCR-positivity persists
Reassess in the relapsed/refractory pathway (next step)

nodes.name: Favorable MRD
nodes.title: Favorable risk: measurable residual disease after consolidation
nodes.description: After high-dose cytarabine consolidation, measurable residual disease (molecular CBF/NPM1 transcripts or multiparameter flow) refines relapse risk and can change post-remission strategy.

nodes.name: Favorable MRD-negative
nodes.title: Favorable, MRD-negative: complete chemotherapy consolidation
nodes.description: MRD-negative favorable-risk disease continues chemotherapy consolidation without transplant.
bullets: Complete the planned cycles of high-dose cytarabine consolidation
Continue serial MRD monitoring (CBF or NPM1 transcripts) through and after consolidation
Reserve allogeneic transplant for MRD reappearance or hematologic relapse
Then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Favorable MRD-positive
nodes.title: Favorable, MRD-positive: escalate / consider transplant
nodes.description: Persistent or rising MRD in favorable-risk disease predicts relapse and shifts management toward transplant.
bullets: Confirm rising MRD on a repeat assay before changing strategy
Refer for allogeneic transplant evaluation - persistent MRD reclassifies a favorable patient toward higher relapse risk
Add or continue the matched targeted agent (e.g. FLT3 inhibitor) where applicable
Enroll on an MRD-directed clinical trial where available; then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: R/R FLT3 response
nodes.title: Relapsed FLT3: response to gilteritinib
nodes.description: Reassess after starting gilteritinib. A response is a bridge to allogeneic transplant; no response or later progression moves to a further line of therapy.

nodes.name: FLT3 salvage to transplant
nodes.title: Relapsed FLT3: bridge to allogeneic transplant
nodes.description: A gilteritinib response in fit patients is consolidated with allogeneic transplant, the main curative option at relapse.
bullets: Proceed to allogeneic transplant once a second remission is achieved on gilteritinib
Give post-transplant FLT3-inhibitor maintenance for FLT3-mutated disease where used
Continue donor search and transplant work-up in parallel with the FLT3 inhibitor
Then move to surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: FLT3 later line
nodes.title: Relapsed FLT3: later-line therapy after a FLT3 inhibitor
nodes.description: After progression on a FLT3 inhibitor, later-line therapy prioritizes trials and non-cross-resistant approaches.
bullets: Clinical-trial enrollment is preferred (FLT3-inhibitor resistance mechanisms, novel combinations)
Venetoclax-based lower-intensity therapy if not previously used
Best supportive care and palliative-care involvement per goals of care
Consider an alternate FLT3 inhibitor only if a distinct resistance profile supports it
